newsitem.title: ITALY: FOCUS-Italy govt approves budget to meet EMU goals.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Italy govt approves budget to meet EMU goals.

text.p: Prime Minsiter Romano Prodi's cabinet approved a mini-budget on Thursday in a bid to rein in the state deficit and earn Italy a place among the first wave of countries signing up to the European single currency.
Prodi said that the package would raise 15.5 trillion lire ($9.2 billion) in 1997 and cut the deficit to three percent of gross domestic product, as demanded by the Maastricht Treaty.
"The government has approved a corrective budget that will enable us to meet the parameters," Prodi told a news conference.

Much of the package is based on accountancy and fiscal changes, with the government expecting to raise six trillion lire alone by forcing companies to pay tax advances on their huge pools of severance payment funds.

Prodi said negotiations with coalition allies and trades unions over welfare reform would start in mid-April, and promised that the eventual deal would be enshrined in the 1998 budget, which has to be approved by the end of this year.

The centre-right opposition bloc, led by Silvio Berlusconi, had called on Prodi to cut social spending in the mini-budget and economists say welfare reform is the only way to secure lasting peace for Italy's heavily indebted economy.
Details of the budget emerged in the press on Thursday ahead of the cabinet's rubber-stamp. The package was roundly criticised by a number of editorials.

"Perhaps the budget will satisfy the Maastricht criteria, but it is basically inadequate to resolve the problems of our country's public finances," top selling financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore wrote in a front page editorial.
Corriere della Sera thought Italy's European Union partners would baulk at the budget.

"The Germans will renounce the single currency rather than share it with a country that might artificially get its deficit to the three percent level but has not found the political consensus needed to resolve long-term problems..." it said.
Prodi said around two-thirds of the measures contained in the mini-budget were of a structural nature and the Treasury said the package would cut some 10.5 trillion lire off the deficit in 1998.
Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said some 2.6 trillion lire would be raised this year by delaying payment of severance handouts to state workers taking early retirement.
A further 1.3 trillion lire will be saved by cutting back ministerial budgets and 500 billion recouped by reducing grants to the state postal service.

On the fiscal side, Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco said three trillion lire would come from the advance payment of certain types of tax and 1.2 trillion lire by simplifying the procedures for paying inheritance tax.

Around 400 billion lire is expected to come by extending an amnesty in which companies or individuals who have violated regulations on social security contributions can regularise their position by paying fines.
Italian financial markets were little moved as full details of the budget emerged.
"There is relief that the coalition was at least able to agree on the budget but disappointment that the content wasn't more meaty," said a bond trader, based in London.
